title: The Rigvidhana
attributionNote: A vidhāna text of the Ṛgveda tradition, ascribed to Śaunaka in the tradition that copied it. Its date is unsettled; like the other vidhānas it is later than the ritual sutras it summarises and earlier than the medieval compendia that quote it as a Ṛgvedic authority. GRETIL's e-text was input by Muneo Tokunaga.
description: The Ṛgvidhāna is the ritual index of the Ṛgveda: for each purpose a sacrifice can serve — long life, children, kingship, rain, the defeat of an enemy, the aversion of misfortune — it names the hymn or the single verse to recite, the deity addressed and the offering that accompanies it. It turns a liturgical collection into a manual of practical uses, chapter by chapter, mantra by mantra.
historicalContext: The vidhāna literature marks the point where the Vedic corpus is treated as a store of effective speech available for chosen ends; the Ṛgvidhāna is one of the earliest such handbooks and was quoted by later ritual and astrological works as the Ṛgveda's own prescription.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: the whole compendium of 749 verses, streamed from GRETIL at read time. Each passage is one verse, addressed as adhyāya.verse, with the section of the adhyāya as its chapter.
